PSED · M3 · discovery support

M3 · Interpretation Brief

Prediction versus observation for the KB-parameterised conformality twin — organized for researcher interpretation. Model: ylilammi_langmuir_channel.

1 · Executive summary

This is a discovery-support brief, not a verdict. M3 organizes evidence and proposes questions; it does not conclude, validate, or discover. Every claim carries an epistemic status. Agreement is not truth; disagreement is not model failure; the measured profiles are fallible extractions, not ground truth. Scientific judgement — choosing among explanations, adopting questions — remains with the researcher, outside this run.
Research question. Does the KB-parameterised Ylilammi channel twin reproduce the measured conformality profile (normalised thickness vs depth; PD50) for in-scope thermal lateral-channel ALD experiments in the current corpus?
40candidate profiles
33admissible comparisons
7non-comparable (refused)
33insufficient evidence
1untested regions
4evidence sources
Diagnosability: weak. 29/33 admissible comparisons come from a single source (10.1039_d0cp03358h); source / extraction / lab systematics cannot be separated from model or parameter behaviour with this ensemble. Because of this, no unique cause is attributed and no anomaly is over-claimed.

2 · What was compared (prediction versus observation)

Model-input provenance summary across the 33 admissible comparisons (363 resolved input instances). Model-default and unresolved inputs are the weakest — the calibration probe (§10 and per-row) then fits the adjustable parameters. Fitted c is a model-specific lumped reaction coefficient c; its ontology mapping to a literature sticking probability is unresolved.

Model-input evidence composition (not a confidence score; parameters are not equally important): 1 directly_resolved · 4 resolved_with_conversion · 5 resolved_by_default · 1 resolved_by_derivation. Load-bearing defaulted/unresolved inputs: pA, gpc, c.
3 · Forward prediction. chain: canonical evidence → resolved runtime input → model attribute → predicted normalised profile → predicted PD50 = 161.7µm (observed PD50 = 192.5µm).
4 · Comparison metrics (descriptive). R²=0.833, shape fit partial, severity moderate. Quantitative agreement: insufficient_evidence (measurement σ unresolved) — not uncertainty-relative and not truth.
5 · Calibration-probe setup. optimizer: Nelder-Mead in a smooth log-sigmoid bounded transform; objective: mean squared error of normalised thickness vs observed depth; residual: predicted_norm(x) - observed_norm(x) at each observed depth; weighting: uniform (unweighted); n_obs=19. active fitted variables: c; fixed: pulse_time_t_p, precursor_partial_pressure_pA.
variablemeaningunitroleinitiallowerupperfittedbound
t_pprecursor pulse timesfixed0.10.10.10.1fixed

6 · Calibration-probe result. t_p (fitted) = 0.1 s [extracted], pA (fixed) = 100 Pa [model_default], derived exposure = pA×t_p = 10 → 10 Pa·s (exposure = pA x t_p (DERIVED; pA fixed, never independently fitted)); c = 0.01 → 0.003161 [inverse_fitted]. SSE 0.06764→0.004783; R² 0.61→0.97.
7 · Bounds & convergence. converged=True, evaluations=8; boundary-limited: False.
8 · Identifiability & provenance caveats. local diagnostic: narrow_isolated_optimum — 1-D c fit; acceptable-c region spans 0% of the log-c range. feasible fitted parameterization, not a unique physical parameter estimate. c is a model-specific lumped reaction coefficient c (ontology mapping unresolved); an inverse-fitted c is never a literature-reported sticking probability. A better fit does not validate the model; a failed fit is not proof of model failure.

3 · What the evidence supports

No forward prediction reached the descriptive shape-agreement threshold, so no supported interpretation is claimed from the forward comparison.
insight the forward twin on DEFAULT kinetics reproduces few profile shapes; a fitted change to the pulse time t_p (where adjustable) and the model-specific lumped coefficient c recovers 12/33 of them, so 'parameterization' is a strongly live explanation for the shortfall — this is a calibration probe (feasible fitted parameterization), not out-of-sample support and not a unique physical estimate

The forward twin on default kinetics does not reproduce most observed profiles. Each discrepancy is left with a plural, non-exclusive explanation space across the six co-equal loci; none is selected. The model is one locus of six — disagreement is not model failure.

7 · Preserved anomalies

preserved anomaly No preserved anomaly can be robustly established under weak diagnosability: with the evidence dominated by a single source and no measurement uncertainty, mundane explanations (parameterization, inputs, measurement, extraction) cannot be ruled out for any discrepancy. The discrepancies are retained as challenged + unresolved (§4, §6) — not explained away, and not over-claimed as anomalies.

10 · Provenance and parameterization exhibit

Observed profiles are digitised extractions (extractor: vision-llm), each a fallible hypothesis. The corpus carries no measurement uncertainty and no calibration flag, so both remain unresolved. Precursor partial-pressure evidence being absent in this processed corpus is NOT a claim that it is absent from the literature — full pressure extraction is not complete.
Parameterization exhibit (calibration probe). Holding the extracted conditions fixed and fitting the ADJUSTABLE model parameter(s): the model-specific lumped reaction coefficient c (always), and the pulse time t_p only when the dose was not extracted. Exposure = pA×t_p is DERIVED, never independently fitted. Bounds are explicit; the fit reports a feasible fitted parameterization, not a unique physical estimate. This evidences the 'parameterization' explanation; it is not out-of-sample support, and an inverse-fitted c is never a literature sticking probability.
